name: BFS-Prover
one_liner: A plain best-first search over Lean tactics, with a model retrained each round on the proofs and compiler errors the search produced.

loop.proposes: Lean 4 tactics for the current proof state, from a language model
loop.judged_by: The Lean 4 compiler through LeanDojo, which runs each tactic and reports success or an error
loop.steers: Best-first search ranks states by log probability; expert iteration retrains on proofs (SFT) and error pairs (DPO)

headline_result: Reaches 72.95% on the miniF2F test set as an accumulative score; the single-run figure is 70.83% +/- 0.89 at a budget of 2048 x 2 x 600 (Lean 4.7.0). The authors say this shows plain best-first search can compete when scaled.
caveat: The 72.95% is a cumulative (union across runs and settings) score, not one fixed-budget run. Its claims date from early 2025 and are compared with provers that used different budgets.
beyond_harness_note: Compiler verdicts retrain the generator between rounds while a search tree is explored; the proofs it outputs are machine-checkable without it.

sources.title: BFS-Prover: Scalable Best-First Tree Search for LLM-based Automatic Theorem Proving

verification.notes: Read abstract and Table 1 text. 72.95% confirmed but it is labelled 'accumulative'; the fixed-budget number is 70.83%. Org inferred from the model's Hugging Face home (ByteDance-Seed) given in the abstract; the author list was not checked for affiliation. Finding that BFS can match fancier search matches the abstract. Org confirmed: paper prints Seed Foundation Code and Applied Machine Learning, ByteDance (review 2026-11-03).
